scenes.title: Cosmic Detective Work
scenes.narration: Astrophysics applies physics to understand the universe, from tiny particles to vast galaxies. It's like being a cosmic detective, analyzing light to uncover secrets of objects billions of light-years away, revealing that 95% of the universe is still unknown.

scenes.title: Decoding Starlight
scenes.narration: Astrophysicists primarily study light and other electromagnetic radiation. This radiation acts as a cosmic messenger, carrying information about an object's temperature, composition, and motion across vast distances, much like a prism splits white light into its constituent colors.

scenes.title: Universe's Building Blocks
scenes.narration: The universe is composed of incredible structures: stars, which are cosmic furnaces; galaxies, massive collections of stars; and exotic phenomena like black holes. These components interact through fundamental forces, shaping the cosmos we observe.

scenes.title: Finding New Worlds
scenes.narration: A major breakthrough is discovering exoplanets, worlds orbiting other stars. Using methods like the transit method, where a planet dims its star's light, we've found over 5,000 exoplanets, some potentially habitable, expanding our search for life.

scenes.title: Expanding Our Cosmic View
scenes.narration: Astrophysics helps us understand the Big Bang, the universe's origin, and the mysteries of dark matter and dark energy. It pushes technological limits, inspiring innovations from medical imaging to satellite communication, while revealing our place in the grand cosmic narrative.
